Use case: style-transfer
Edit target: original first town map from a Chinese historical RPG, centered in a 1536x1024 canvas with 154px black side gutters. Generate a complete new art-direction image, same canvas and map boundaries. Preserve the fixed original overhead oblique camera, exact building positions and footprint sizes, doors, paths, outer wall and all landmarks. Do not crop. Do not turn the town into an isometric diamond. No characters, UI, captions or new objects.
Map content: seven compact two-story Chinese buildings with blue tiled roofs and red lanterns (two at upper left/center left, one upper right, one middle left, one middle right, two bottom); red and ivory perimeter walls with north central exit; green-gray stone paving; two circular stone wells; four green trees including the lower-right partial tree; wooden crates and jars; a white sail or awning beside the middle-right building; narrow central lower blue water channel with stone edging and crossings; larger water section at bottom right. Preserve all passages and water outlines. Shops have small signs, preserve their placement. Make doors, paving, trees and water immediately readable at phone size. Keep floor detail quieter than buildings. Do not copy blurry pixel noise. Reinterpret forms with clear structural detail. Every object in one consistent style.

Style: Unreal Engine 5 quality stylized-realistic 3D game environment. Physically based blue glazed roof tiles, carved timber, lacquered red pillars, soft luminous lanterns in daylight, tactile stone paving, lush detailed foliage and convincing reflective blue water. Soft daylight global illumination, clean readable objects. Match original overhead camera. No depth of field, bloom, fog, lens distortion or excessively dark lighting. Not an actual engine screenshot.
